column3: The Hebrew names the soul as the one who loves (“whom my soul loves”), whereas the BSB says “the one I love.”
The Hebrew names the soul as the one who loves (“whom my soul loves”), whereas the BSB says “the one I love.”
In the Hebrew the watchmen found her; the BSB makes her the subject of “encountered.” The BSB’s question does not mention the soul.
The animals are connected with or, rather than “and”; the love itself chooses, rather than the impersonal “time is right.”
Columns of smoke is plural, rather than “a column.”
The object is called his bed or couch; “mightiest” adds a superlative not expressed in the Hebrew.
They hold swords, rather than the first clause saying “skilled with the sword”; the thigh is explicitly named.
In the Hebrew his mother crowned him; the BSB says the crown was “bestowed.” The Hebrew joins the two descriptions of the day with “and,” which the BSB replaces with a dash.
